title: Module quiz: Managed and self-hosted agents

questions.stem: A hospital group must keep patient files inside its own network but wants Anthropic to run the agent loop. Which setup fits?

options.text: A cloud sandbox with `limited` networking and a few allowed hosts
options.says: Ruled out because "By default tools run in Anthropic's sandboxes.", so the files would be processed on Anthropic's side.

options.text: A self-hosted sandbox whose tools execute on local machines
options.says: The page says "Self-hosted sandboxes keep the orchestration on Anthropic's side but move tool execution into infrastructure you control", and the group still owns the image and the egress rules.

options.text: The Messages API with the files pasted into each prompt
options.says: Ruled out because "You write the loop on the Messages API.", and the group wants Anthropic to run the loop.

options.text: The Agent SDK running in the group's own process
options.says: Ruled out because "You embed Claude Code's loop with the Agent SDK, in a process you operate.", so the group, not Anthropic, would run it.

questions.stem: A developer migrates an Agent SDK service whose `can_use_tool` callback approved reads and refused pushes. What replaces that callback in Managed Agents?

options.text: A per-tool permission policy, with confirmations sent as events
options.says: The first page says `permission_mode` and `can_use_tool` "become a per-tool permission policy", and a paused call is answered with a `user.tool_confirmation` event.

options.text: The `ClaudeAgentOptions` object, created again for every run
options.says: Ruled out because the migration "becomes an agent created once" from that object.

options.text: The environment's `networking` field, which approves each command
options.says: Ruled out because `networking` controls the sandbox's outbound traffic, and "so `networking` does not govern them" for the search and fetch tools.

options.text: A model override on the session that removes the tool
options.says: Ruled out because an override "must list every tool the session should have", and removing a tool is not an approval step.

questions.stem: A product relays customers' messages to an agent as `user.message` events and sets the toolset to `auto`. What is the risk?

options.text: Their text counts as the operator's own intent when a call is judged
options.says: The page says "If you relay untrusted end-user input in `user.message` events, the server reads that input as your intent too."

options.text: The server ignores `user.message` events once a policy is set
options.says: Ruled out because what you post in `user.message` events "counts as your intent", so the server reads it.

options.text: Every call pauses until a person has confirmed it
options.says: Ruled out because "`auto` is not a human checkpoint", and a safe call "runs before anyone sees it".

options.text: A denied call can be overridden by the client with a confirmation
options.says: Ruled out because a denied call is final: "your client cannot override the denial."

questions.stem: A finance team wants to know what one long session's reported cost contains. Which items make up that total?

options.text: Model tokens, event-history storage and disk space
options.says: Ruled out because "The documentation lists these three items and no other.", and storage and disk are not among them.

options.text: Model tokens alone, with sandbox time left free
options.says: Ruled out because running time is priced: "Session running time, at $0.08 per hour".

options.text: Model tokens, web searches and running time
options.says: The page says the total is "model tokens at each model's list price, web searches at $10 per 1,000", and "Session running time, at $0.08 per hour".

options.text: Model tokens and web searches, with running time billed apart
options.says: Ruled out because running time is one of the three items of "the total is its list cost", not a separate bill.
